summary: The 49ers routed the Cowboys 42-10 on Sunday Night Football on Oct. 8, 2023 at Levi's Stadium, improving to 5-0. Brock Purdy threw four touchdowns, three to George Kittle, while Dak Prescott threw three second-half interceptions. The note is a live blog with drive-by-drive updates plus broadcast and start-time info.
one_line: San Francisco crushed Dallas 42-10 on Sunday Night Football behind Brock Purdy's four touchdowns and a dominant defense led by Fred Warner.
key_facts: The 49ers beat the Cowboys 42-10 on Sunday, Oct. 8, 2023 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif.
Brock Purdy threw four touchdowns, including three to George Kittle; the fourth went to Kyle Juszczyk.
Christian McCaffrey scored a touchdown for a 14th consecutive game.
Fred Warner finished with an interception, a sack and a forced fumble.
Dak Prescott threw three interceptions in the second half, to Tashaun Gipson, Fred Warner and Oren Burks.
San Francisco is now 5-0 and doesn't face a team with a winning record until Week 10.
Dallas sits two games behind the Eagles in the NFC East.
The 49ers have knocked the Cowboys out of the playoffs in each of the last two seasons.
Sam Darnold entered for the 49ers with more than 12 minutes remaining; Cooper Rush played for Dallas.
KaVontae Turpin caught a 26-yard touchdown pass from Prescott for Dallas's only touchdown; Brandon Aubrey kicked a 50-yard field goal.
Randy Gregory, a new 49ers acquisition, was inactive against his former team.
The game aired on NBC with Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth and Melissa Stark; kickoff was 8:20 p.m. ET.
